questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14065207/assets/83b23d8138091a931d14854b197752d25d8149ee8914a70b8db73b6c2369c888.png)

Given the graph of $y=f(x)$ above, find the value of 
${\int }_{-2}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x.$
questions.worked_solution:
The graph consists of $2$ parts: the line segment for $x\in [-2,3)$ and the arc of the semi-circle for $x\in [3,5].$ So, we can use the additive property of integrals to get

$$
{\int }_{-2}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{-2}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{3}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{2}}.
$$

- The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-2,3).$ The corresponding region is a rectangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =b\cdot h \\  & =5\cdot 2 \\  & =10.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [3,5].$ The corresponding region is a semi-circle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}\pi {r}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\pi \cdot (1)^{2} \\  & =\frac{\pi }{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={A}_{1}+{A}_{2} \\  & =10+\frac{\pi }{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

If the graph of $y=f(x)$ is shown above, then

${\int }_{-4}^{1}f(x)\,\text{d}x=$

questions.worked_solution:
The graph consists of $2$ parts: the arc of the semi-circle for $x\in [-4,-2]$ and the line segment for $x\in (-2,1].$ So, we can use the additive property of integrals to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-4}^{1}f(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{-4}^{-2}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{-2}^{1}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-4,-2].$ The corresponding region is a semi-circle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}\pi {r}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\pi \cdot (1)^{2} \\  & =\frac{\pi }{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in (-2,1].$ The corresponding region is a trapezoid, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}(a+b)h \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(2+1)\cdot 3 \\  & =\frac{9}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-4}^{1}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={A}_{1}+{A}_{2} \\  & =\frac{\pi }{2}+\frac{9}{2} \\  & =\frac{\pi +9}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14065207/assets/06ace831b877406e48fe8f1ab38a7244e7ade878d7c77b99d8230f40ad307207.png)

The graph of $y=f(x),$ shown above, consists of four line segments. Then,

${\int }_{-6}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x=$
{{field-1}}.
questions.worked_solution:
The graph consists of four parts: the line segment for $x\in [-6,-3],$ the line segment for $x\in (-3,0],$ the line segment for $x\in (0,2],$ and the line segment for $x\in (2,5].$ Therefore, we can write the required integral as follows:

$$
{\int }_{-6}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{-6}^{-3}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{-3}^{0}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{2}}+{{{\int }_{0}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{3}}+{{{\int }_{2}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{4}}.
$$

- The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-6,-3].$ The corresponding region is a right triangle, so

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}(bh) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}3(3) \\  & =4.5.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in (-3,0].$ The corresponding region is a rectangle, so

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =bh \\  & =3\cdot 1 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $3$rd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in (0,2].$ The corresponding region is a trapezoid, so

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{3} & =\frac{1}{2}(a+b)h \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(4+2)(2) \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $4$th integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in (2,5].$ The corresponding region is a right triangle, so

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{4} & =\frac{1}{2}(bh) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}3(6) \\  & =9.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-6}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={A}_{1}+{A}_{2}+{A}_{3}+{A}_{4} \\  & =4.5+3+6+9 \\  & =22.5.\end{aligned}
$$

The graph $y=f(x),$ shown above, consists of two line segments. Then,

${\int }_{-5}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x=$
{{field-1}}.
questions.worked_solution:
We divide the interval of integration into $3$ regions: the line segment for $x\in [-5,0],$ the line segment for $x\in (0,3],$ and the line segment for $x\in [3,5].$ Therefore, we can write the required integral as follows:

$$
{\int }_{-5}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{-5}^{0}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{0}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{2}}+{{{\int }_{3}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{-{A}_{3}}.
$$

- The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-5,0].$   The corresponding region is a trapezoid, so

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}(a+b)h \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(1+4)(5) \\  & =\frac{25}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in (0,3].$    The corresponding region is a trapezoid, so

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}(a+b)h \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(3+0)(3) \\  & =\frac{9}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $3$rd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [3,5].$   The corresponding region is a trapezoid, so

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{3} & =\frac{1}{2}(a+b)h \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(0+2)(2) \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we have

$$
{\int }_{3}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-{A}_{3}=-2.
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-5}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={A}_{1}+{A}_{2}-{A}_{3} \\  & =\frac{25}{2}+\frac{9}{2}-2 \\  & =15.\end{aligned}
$$

If the graph of $y=f(x)$ is shown above, then

${\int }_{-6}^{6}f(x)\,\text{d}x=$
{{field-1}}.
questions.worked_solution:
The graph consists of $3$ parts: the line segment for $x\in [-6,-3),$ the arc of the semi-circle for $x\in (-3,3),$ and the line segment for $x\in (3,6].$ So, we can use the additive property of integrals to get

$$
{\int }_{-6}^{6}f(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{-6}^{-3}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{-3}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{2}}+{{{\int }_{3}^{6}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{3}}.
$$

- The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-6,-3).$ The corresponding region is a trapezoid, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}(a+b)h \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(4+1)\cdot 3 \\  & =\frac{15}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in (-3,3).$ The corresponding region is a combination of a semi-circle of radius $3$ and a rectangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =bh+\frac{1}{2}\pi {r}^{2} \\  & =6(1)+\frac{1}{2}\pi (3)^{2} \\  & =6+\frac{9\pi }{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $3$rd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in (3,6].$ The corresponding region is a trapezoid, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{3} & =\frac{1}{2}(a+b)h \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(1+2)\cdot 3 \\  & =\frac{9}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-6}^{6}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={A}_{1}+{A}_{2}+{A}_{3} \\  & =\frac{15}{2}+6+\frac{9\pi }{2}+\frac{9}{2} \\  & =18+\frac{9\pi }{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
